study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Timothy Lawn et al., Communications Biology, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience) and UCLA-LA5c (UCLA phenomics dataset, ref 120/Poldrack 2016).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The data utilised is from two existing datasets: CamCAN ageing and UCLA phenomics... UCLA phenomics dataset (ref. 120, available from https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds000030/versions/1.0.0)

answer.UCLA-LA5c: normative training/testing (HC) and patient for clinical research (SCHZ, BPD, ADHD)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Cam-CAN and UCLA HC were used for normative model training (70%) and testing (30%). UCLA patient cohorts (SCHZ, BPD, ADHD) were used for clinical research application of the models.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Normative models were trained on 70% of the healthy control data across both UCLA and CamCAN datasets and tested on the remaining 30%... UCLA... including healthy individuals as well as data from three clinical cohorts (Schizophrenia - SCHZ, bipolar disorder - BPD, and ADHD).

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative models (HBR for each ROI and receptor system) used a total of 607 healthy controls. The training phase included 424 HCs (346 from CamCAN, 78 from UCLA).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Following quality control exclusions, imaging data of a total of 607 healthy subjects (CamCAN: N = 496, UCLA: N = 111) were included in the analysis... resulting in CamCAN = 346/150 and UCLA = 78/33 train/test subdivisions.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Lawn2024.pdf.md: Results / Demographics; Methods / Normative modelling

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean and pooled SD calculated for the overall HC group (N=607) from CamCAN (N=496, 52.3 ± 18.3) and UCLA (N=111, 31.2 ± 8.7). Age ranges are 18-87 for CamCAN and 21-50 for UCLA.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: CamCAN: N = 496, Mean age (SD) = 52.3 (18.3)... UCLA: N = 111, Mean age (SD) = 31.2 (8.7)... CamCAN... 18-87 years old... UCLA... participants were aged between 21-50.
